[P2] Salem witch trials
The Salem witch trials were a series of hearings and prosecutions of people accused of witchcraft in colonial Massachusetts between February 1692 and May 1693 . The trials resulted in the executions of twenty people , fourteen of them women , and all but one by hanging . Five others ( including two infant children ) died in prison . Twelve other women had previously been executed in Massachusetts and Connecticut during the 17th century . Despite being generally known as the Salem Witch Trials , the preliminary hearings in 1692 were conducted in several towns : Salem Village ( now Danvers ) , Salem Town , Ipswich , and Andover . The most infamous trials were conducted by the Court of Oyer and Terminer in 1692 in Salem Town . The episode is one of Colonial America 's most notorious cases of mass hysteria .

[P3] Mergentheim witch trials
The Mergentheim witch trials was a witch trial taking place in Mergentheim in Germany between 1628 and 1631 . It resulted in the death of 126 people ; 122 executions , four died during torture . It belonged to the great wave of witch hunt taking place in South Western Germany during the Thirty Years ' War . It is one of the most well documented of the mass witch trials of South Western Germany . Its perhaps most known victim was Thomas Schreiber ( innkeeper ) .
